BuiltinExternalLayouts.name: BuiltinExternalLayouts
BuiltinExternalLayouts.description: External layouts hold instances placed apart from a scene, using the objects and layers of the scene they are associated with. Their instances are not created when the scene starts: the scene creates them when needed, with the action to create objects from an external layout, at their editor positions (offset by an origin), on their layer, with their size, angle, Z order, visibility and instance variables. The objects and layers used must exist in the scene creating them (any external layout of the project can be loaded, not only the ones associated with the scene). Nothing is removed first: creating the same external layout again duplicates its objects, so delete the previous instances (for example the previous level) before loading new ones. Typical uses: the levels of a game built in a single scene (one external layout per level, loaded at the beginning of the scene according to a variable), a room or an enemy wave spawned on demand. For a UI panel, a custom object is usually a better fit (it is reusable, resizable and can hold its own logic); use an external layout for a simple, one-off UI screen.
